This was the final thing we grepped because of the reports related to FDroid repos. We saw more broken pipes, but expected them to being unrelated, we noticed later that also normal file transfers fail. I'll check the logs again with this information.

Note: `2021/06/02 06:12:09 routers/repo/http.go:556:serviceRPC() [E] Fail to serve RPC(upload-pack) in /data/git/gitea-repositories/hjacobs/kube-resource-report.git: exit status 128 - fatal: the remote end hung up unexpectedly` - this log line is most likely unrelated and means the client side hung up (we also suspected the reverse proxy or something). We tried looking for correlations between those messages and the actual issues, but found none.

Hmm, the canceling file downloads don't seem to appear in the logs, will play with the loglevels once more.

But basically, we're seeing this broken pipe issue, on slow throughput or when halting the download (I'm using ctrl+z and fg from time to time when reproducing locally when I don't want to throttle my full machine)

We were already looking for some timeout, but found none left to configure.
Using haproxy for connections to other backends (e.g. file serving from nginx) works fine. Direct access to Gitea via the local port results in the same issue.

Oh and I just noticed the error log from OP is translated, the English version would look like
~~~
error: 7158 bytes of body are still expected29 MiB | 487.00 KiB/s
fetch-pack: unexpected disconnect while reading sideband packet
fatal: early EOF
fatal: index-pack failed
~~~

Ok your logs imply to me that the response writer is being closed independently of the upload pack. 

So ... If we're sure it's not coming from a proxy it must be being closed further down within gitea.

Now, we know that long running connections are allowed because the event stream doesn't have this problem. So there's maybe something that the event stream is setting on the response that is preventing this early close?

I guess it would be helpful to know if you're running with the inbuilt gzip handler or other config?

In particular we set:

 https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/c1ff59c1cd51da6fcc47d31ca84932e9bccced92/routers/events/events.go#L29

Which we don't set in http.

So a good guess might be to set that after this line here:

https://github.com/go-gitea/gitea/blob/c1ff59c1cd51da6fcc47d31ca84932e9bccced92/routers/repo/http.go#L439

We didn't change the GZIP config. In case you have questions about the codeberg config and don't want to wait for a reply, you can usually look at https://codeberg.org/Codeberg/build-deploy-gitea/src/branch/master/etc/gitea/conf/app.ini - in case this is easier for you.

Please keep in mind that normal file transfer seemed to show this very same issue (e.g. downloading a big file from gitea/public). Maybe a similiarity between repo and other connections (public serving + most likely file attachments) gives you a hint?

I think it's all similar as I don't think we set the keep alive header on those either so it's worth checking if the above suggestion solves things.

If it does then we can add in the keep alive command elsewhere or everywhere. 

If it doesn't then at least we know it's not that.

Well, nevermind, I just finished the bisect, have a look at this commit: 41422f0df06be53d9ae8e16e385f03b81bd47f51

> Add timeout to writing to responses (#15831) (#15872)
>
> Backport #15831
>
> In #15826 it has become apparent that there are a few occasions when a response can
> hang during writing, and because there is no timeout go will happily just block
> interminably. This PR adds a fixed 5 second timeout to all writes to a connection.
>
> Fix #15826
>
> Signed-off-by: Andrew Thornton <art27@cantab.net>

Sounds obvious ...
Aha!

So I think we still need this timeout - otherwise go will happily hold on to the connections when the connection is blocked.

I guess we just need to increase the length of this timeout.

So through compiling you can trial a few different values as I state in the PR:

LDFLAGS="-X \"code.gitea.io/gitea/modules/graceful.PerWriteWriteTimeout=30s\""

~~one other option is whether we should just tie the ResponseWriter to the request context?~~ Nope that won't work. We just need to adjust the PerWriteWriteTimeout to something larger possibly temporarily for these requests. I don't think setting it to 0 would be safe.

Yes, we're doing exactly this right now.

I think, with this we mainly shift the curve, kinda like a threshold how slow a connection can become ... not sure if there is a better solution like knowing exactly if it's still alive or something ...

I also don't quite know the impact of the main issue. Would it be an option to set it really high, like a few minutes, so that only really stale connections are cleaned? Personally, I know that it's sometimes convenient when a network transfer continues, even when the connection was disrupted for a short time.

So I think there is some kind of function: the larger the blob to transfer and the slower the connection, the easier this will be hit. Remember I was running into this with 50KB/s transfer on a 100MB file after 5 seconds. I'd imagine that when you increase this to 60 seconds, but my transfer wouldn't have been finished, this would result in the same issue, but later (will try). With higher bandwidth but larger data, this should stay proportional.

OK, let's do a heuristic adjustment.

Couple of ideas:

1. Simplest: Store the last deadline that we set 
    * Minimum deadline is Now()+ 5s
    * If previous deadline has not passed use it instead of now + 5s 
    * PROBLEMS: This could be lead to very very long timeouts - but I guess that is reasonable. 
    * There's also no depenedence on the size of slice being written or how much written just on how many times written
2. Take account of what's about to be written plus the last timeout
    * Minimum basic timeout is 5s 
    * Timeout: is 2.5s + 2s * len(towrite)/1024 + previous deadline if this is longer
3. Take account of the amount written:
    * Minimum basic timeout is 5s
    * Timeout: is 2s * len(towrite + written)/1024 + previous deadline
